symptom: PC1 cannot ping PC2 in the same VLAN across Switch-1 and Switch-2
topology_note: PC1 (192.168.10.10/24) on S1 Fa0/1 (VLAN 10). PC2 (192.168.10.20/24) on S2 Fa0/1 (VLAN 10). Trunk link between S1 Gi0/1 and S2 Gi0/1.
show_output_evidence: S1# show interfaces trunk -> Gi0/1 802.1q trunking 10,20; S2# show interfaces trunk -> Gi0/1 802.1q trunking 20,30 (VLAN 10 missing from allowed list)
expected_fault: VLAN 10 is not permitted on the trunk link of Switch-2 (switchport trunk allowed vlan missing VLAN 10)
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad CCNA SRWE Lab 2.2.13 (Troubleshoot VLANs and Trunks)

symptom: Native VLAN mismatch error in Syslog; traffic between VLAN 1 and native untagged VLAN leaking
topology_note: S1 Gi0/1 connects to S2 Gi0/1. S1 trunk native VLAN configured as 99; S2 trunk native VLAN remains default 1.
show_output_evidence: %CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on GigabitEthernet0/1 (99), with S2 GigabitEthernet0/1 (1). S1# show interfaces Gi0/1 switchport -> Trunking Native Mode VLAN: 99; S2# show interfaces Gi0/1 switchport -> Trunking Native Mode VLAN: 1
expected_fault: Native VLAN mismatch between interconnected switch trunk interfaces (S1 uses VLAN 99, S2 uses default VLAN 1)
reference_source_note: Adapted from Cisco IOS Switching Command Reference & NetAcad SRWE Lab 2.2.13

symptom: PC in Accounting department cannot communicate with local gateway or file server
topology_note: PC3 (192.168.30.15/24) connected to S1 Fa0/5. Accounting subnet is VLAN 30.
show_output_evidence: S1# show vlan brief -> Port Fa0/5 is assigned to VLAN 1 (default), while VLAN 30 (Accounting) exists with ports Fa0/10-12.
expected_fault: Access port Fa0/5 is incorrectly assigned to default VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 30
reference_source_note: Adapted from CCNA ITN Lab 10.4.3 & SRWE Lab 2.1.4 (VLAN Configuration)

symptom: Router-on-a-Stick inter-VLAN routing fails between Sales (VLAN 10) and Marketing (VLAN 20)
topology_note: Router R1 Gi0/0.10 and Gi0/0.20 subinterfaces connect to Switch S1 Gi0/1 (Trunk).
show_output_evidence: R1# show running-config interface Gi0/0.10 -> encapsulation dot1Q 20 (encapsulation tag 20 set on subinterface .10 with IP 192.168.10.1); Gi0/0.20 -> encapsulation dot1Q 20
expected_fault: Subinterface G0/0.10 was configured with wrong 802.1Q tag (tag 20 instead of tag 10), causing VLAN 10 frame drop
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad SRWE Lab 3.4.5 (Troubleshoot Inter-VLAN Routing)

symptom: Host PC cannot ping default gateway; local ARP table shows incomplete for gateway IP
topology_note: PC1 IP 192.168.1.50/24, configured gateway 192.168.1.1. Router R1 interface Gi0/0 is the intended gateway.
show_output_evidence: C:\> arp -a -> 192.168.1.1 incomplete; R1# show ip interface brief -> GigabitEthernet0/0 192.168.1.1 YES manual administratively down down
expected_fault: Router default gateway interface Gi0/0 is administratively shut down (missing 'no shutdown')
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad ITN Lab 17.7.6 (Troubleshoot Connectivity Issues)

symptom: Workstation cannot communicate outside local subnet; can ping neighbors on same switch
show_output_evidence: PC-A> ipconfig /all -> Default Gateway: 172.16.10.254; R1# show ip interface brief -> Gi0/0/0 172.16.10.1 up up. Ping from PC-A to 172.16.10.254 times out.
expected_fault: Host workstation has incorrect default gateway IP configured (172.16.10.254 instead of 172.16.10.1)
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad ITN Lab 11.5.5 (Subnetting & Host Gateway Troubleshooting)

symptom: HSRP active/standby state flaps; dual active routers claiming virtual IP 192.168.1.254
topology_note: Router R1 (Gi0/1: 192.168.1.2) and Router R2 (Gi0/1: 192.168.1.3). HSRP Group 1 Virtual IP 192.168.1.254.
show_output_evidence: R1# show standby brief -> Grp 1 Pri 110 State Active Active: local Standby: unknown; R2# show standby brief -> Grp 2 Pri 100 State Active Active: local Standby: unknown
expected_fault: HSRP group number mismatch (R1 configured under 'standby 1', R2 configured under 'standby 2')
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad SRWE Lab 9.2.9 (Troubleshoot HSRP)

symptom: HSRP standby router fails to take over active role when primary router metric/priority degrades
topology_note: R1 priority 110 without preempt. R2 priority 105 with preempt. R1 rebooted/recovered with priority 90 after tracking.
show_output_evidence: R1# show standby brief -> Grp 1 Pri 90 State Active (Preempt disabled); R2# show standby brief -> Grp 1 Pri 105 State Standby (Preempt enabled)
expected_fault: Primary router lacks 'standby 1 preempt' or secondary router priority tracking is misaligned
reference_source_note: Adapted from Cisco HSRP Configuration Guide & NetAcad SRWE Module 9

symptom: Clients in Branch LAN receive APIPA address (169.254.x.x) instead of corporate DHCP scope
topology_note: Clients on VLAN 10 connected to Switch S1. Central DHCP Server on 10.1.100.10 connected via Router R1 Gi0/0.
show_output_evidence: PC1> ipconfig -> Autoconfiguration IPv4: 169.254.45.12; R1# show running-config interface Gi0/0.10 -> interface GigabitEthernet0/0.10 has no 'ip helper-address' command.
expected_fault: Missing DHCP relay agent ('ip helper-address 10.1.100.10') on the client-facing router subinterface
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad SRWE Lab 7.4.2 (Troubleshoot DHCPv4)

symptom: New devices cannot obtain DHCP lease; existing devices with active leases work normally
topology_note: Router R1 acts as local DHCP server for pool 192.168.20.0/24 (Scope: 192.168.20.1 - 192.168.20.254).
show_output_evidence: R1# show ip dhcp pool LAN-POOL -> Total addresses: 5, Leased addresses: 5, Excluded: 249; R1# show ip dhcp binding -> 5 bindings listed; pool exhausted.
expected_fault: DHCP pool address starvation due to overly broad 'ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.20.6 192.168.20.254'
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad SRWE Lab 7.2.7 (Implement DHCPv4 on IOS)

symptom: Client obtains DHCP address but receives IP conflict error pop-up; connectivity drops
topology_note: PC1 receives 192.168.1.100 via DHCP. Network printer PR1 has static IP 192.168.1.100.
show_output_evidence: R1# show ip dhcp conflict -> Detection method: Ping, IP address: 192.168.1.100; PC1 Event Log: 'The system detected an address conflict for IP address 192.168.1.100'
expected_fault: Static IP assigned to printer overlaps with DHCP pool scope without being excluded with 'ip dhcp excluded-address'
reference_source_note: Adapted from Cisco IOS IP Addressing Services Command Reference

symptom: DHCP Offer packets dropped after enabling switch security; clients cannot obtain IP
topology_note: Clients on S1 access ports. S1 connects to DHCP server via trunk port Gi0/1. DHCP snooping enabled on S1.
show_output_evidence: S1# show ip dhcp snooping -> DHCP snooping is enabled on VLAN 10; S1# show ip dhcp snooping binding -> 0 bindings; S1# show ip dhcp snooping | section Gi0/1 -> Trusted: No
expected_fault: Trunk uplink Gi0/1 facing the DHCP server is untrusted in DHCP snooping ('ip dhcp snooping trust' missing)
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad SRWE Lab 10.4.3 (Troubleshoot LAN Security)

symptom: Workstations can ping external IP (8.8.8.8) but cannot browse websites using domain names
topology_note: Host PC configured with static IP 192.168.1.20/24, Gateway 192.168.1.1, DNS 192.168.1.250. Valid DNS is 192.168.1.2.
show_output_evidence: PC> ping 8.8.8.8 -> Reply from 8.8.8.8: bytes=32 time=12ms; PC> nslookup cisco.com -> DNS request timed out, Server: UnKnown, Address: 192.168.1.250
expected_fault: Incorrect DNS server IP configured on host workstation (192.168.1.250 instead of 192.168.1.2)
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad ITN Lab 17.8.3 (Troubleshooting Challenge)

symptom: Internal DNS queries fail across perimeter firewall/router; local hosts cannot resolve names
topology_note: Internal clients on 10.0.1.0/24 query external DNS server 208.67.222.222 via edge router R1.
show_output_evidence: PC> nslookup example.com -> DNS request timed out; R1# show access-lists 101 -> 10 permit tcp 10.0.1.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 53 (0 matches), 20 deny ip any any (450 matches)
expected_fault: ACL 101 only permits TCP port 53; UDP port 53 (standard DNS query protocol) is blocked by implicit deny
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad ENSA Lab 4.4.4 (Troubleshoot IPv4 ACLs)

symptom: Router cannot resolve hostnames in CLI; ping server1.lab.local fails with Unknown host
topology_note: Router R1 management CLI trying to ping internal syslog/FTP server by hostname.
show_output_evidence: R1# ping server1.lab.local -> Translating "server1.lab.local"...domain server (255.255.255.255) % Unrecognized host; R1# show running-config | include name-server -> no 'ip name-server' configured
expected_fault: Missing 'ip name-server <DNS_IP>' and 'ip domain-lookup' configuration on the Cisco IOS router
reference_source_note: Adapted from Cisco IOS Basic System Management Command Reference

symptom: Branch router R1 cannot reach HQ server subnet (10.20.0.0/16); pings from R1 drop
topology_note: Branch R1 connects to ISP via Serial0/0/0 (198.51.100.1/30). Next-hop is ISP Serial0/0/0 (198.51.100.2).
show_output_evidence: R1# show ip route -> Gateway of last resort is not set; 198.51.100.0/30 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0; No static or default route exists for 10.20.0.0/16
expected_fault: Missing static route or default route ('ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 198.51.100.2') to upstream router
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad SRWE Lab 14.3.5 (Troubleshoot Static and Default Routes)

symptom: Static route installed on Router R1 is inactive and does not appear in the routing table
show_output_evidence: R1# show ip route static -> (empty); R1# show running-config | include ip route -> ip route 172.16.1.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.1.2; R1# show ip route 10.0.1.2 -> % Network not in table
expected_fault: Static route next-hop IP 10.0.1.2 is unreachable/unresolvable (recursive routing failure; next-hop typo)
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad SRWE Module 14 & CCNA Routing Protocols Guide

symptom: OSPF neighbor adjacency stuck in EXSTART/EXCHANGE state between R1 and R2
show_output_evidence: R1# show ip ospf neighbor -> Neighbor ID 2.2.2.2 Pri 1 State EXSTART/DROTHER Dead Time 00:00:33; R1# show interfaces Gi0/0 -> MTU 1500 bytes; R2# show interfaces Gi0/0 -> MTU 1400 bytes
expected_fault: Interface MTU mismatch between OSPF neighbors (R1 MTU 1500 vs R2 MTU 1400 prevents DBD exchange)
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad ENSA Lab 2.7.1 (Troubleshoot Single-Area OSPFv2)

symptom: OSPF neighbor adjacency fails to form; no neighbor listed in show ip ospf neighbor
topology_note: R1 Gi0/0 connects to R2 Gi0/0. Both routers configured with 'router ospf 1'.
show_output_evidence: R1# show ip ospf interface Gi0/0 -> Area 0, Hello 10, Dead 40; R2# show ip ospf interface Gi0/0 -> Area 1, Hello 10, Dead 40; R1# show ip ospf neighbor -> (empty)
expected_fault: OSPF Area ID mismatch on connecting link (R1 interface in Area 0, R2 interface in Area 1)
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad ENSA Lab 2.7.2 (Troubleshoot OSPFv2 Neighbor Relationships)

symptom: OSPF neighbor adjacency forms, but R2 LAN subnet (192.168.20.0/24) is not advertised to R1
topology_note: R2 Gi0/1 connects to LAN 192.168.20.0/24. R2 runs OSPF process 1.
show_output_evidence: R1# show ip route ospf -> (empty); R2# show running-config | section router ospf -> router ospf 1, network 10.1.1.0 0.0.0.3 area 0 (missing 192.168.20.0 network statement)
expected_fault: Missing 'network 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255 area 0' statement (or interface ospf activation) on R2
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad ENSA Lab 2.7.1 (Single-Area OSPFv2 Configuration)

symptom: OSPF neighbor hello packets ignored; adjacency drops after dead timer expires
topology_note: R1 Gi0/1 connects to R2 Gi0/1. Hello timer modified on R1.
show_output_evidence: R1# show ip ospf interface Gi0/1 -> Hello 5, Dead 20; R2# show ip ospf interface Gi0/1 -> Hello 10, Dead 40; Syslog: %OSPF-5-ADJCHG: Process 1, Nbr 2.2.2.2 on Gi0/1 from FULL to DOWN, Neighbor Down: Dead timer expired
expected_fault: OSPF Hello and Dead timer mismatch between adjacent interfaces (5/20 vs 10/40)
reference_source_note: Adapted from Cisco OSPF Neighbor States Reference & NetAcad ENSA Lab 2.7.2

symptom: HR VLAN cannot access Web Server in Server Farm; all HTTP traffic times out
topology_note: HR Subnet: 192.168.10.0/24. Web Server: 172.16.50.100 (Port 80/443). ACL 100 applied inbound on R1 Gi0/0.
show_output_evidence: R1# show access-lists 100 -> 10 deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 any (245 matches), 20 permit tcp any host 172.16.50.100 eq 80; R1# show running-config interface Gi0/0 -> ip access-group 100 in
expected_fault: ACL statement order error: Broad 'deny ip 192.168.10.0' rule is evaluated before the specific 'permit tcp' rule
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad ENSA Lab 4.4.4 (Troubleshoot IPv4 ACLs)

symptom: Branch network cannot SSH into Edge Router management interface; pings succeed
topology_note: Admin PC (192.168.1.100) attempting SSH to Router R1 (192.168.1.1).
show_output_evidence: Admin-PC> ssh -l admin 192.168.1.1 -> Connection refused/timed out; R1# show running-config | section line vty -> line vty 0 4, access-class 21 in; R1# show access-lists 21 -> 10 permit 192.168.2.0 0.0.0.255
expected_fault: Standard ACL 21 applied to VTY lines permits only 192.168.2.0/24; 192.168.1.100 is blocked by implicit deny
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad ITN Lab 16.5.1 & ENSA Lab 4.2.7 (Securing VTY with ACL)

symptom: Outbound traffic from Engineering VLAN blocked at border router; show access-lists shows hits on deny
topology_note: Engineering Subnet 10.10.0.0/16. ACL 110 placed on R1 Gi0/1 (Outbound to ISP).
show_output_evidence: R1# show access-lists 110 -> 10 permit ip 10.10.0.0 0.0.255.255 any (0 matches), 20 deny ip any any (132 matches); R1# show running-config interface Gi0/1 -> ip access-group 110 out
expected_fault: Wildcard mask error in ACL 110 ('0.0.255.255' represents /16 inverted, but engineering subnet is /24 '10.10.0.0 0.0.0.255' or subnets mismatched)
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad ENSA Lab 4.4.4 & Cisco ACL Wildcard Mask Reference

symptom: Web clients cannot reach intranet HTTPS server after applying outbound ACL on router interface
topology_note: Clients 192.168.1.0/24 accessing internal Web Server 10.0.0.50 on port 443.
show_output_evidence: R1# show access-lists 105 -> 10 permit tcp any host 10.0.0.50 eq 443; R1# show running-config interface Gi0/0 -> ip access-group 105 in (traffic from server returning to clients has no permit)
expected_fault: ACL lacks return traffic rule ('permit tcp any any established') or was placed in the wrong interface direction (inbound on LAN instead of DMZ)
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad ENSA Lab 4.4.4 (Troubleshoot Extended ACLs)

symptom: Internal LAN clients cannot access Internet; ping to public IP 203.0.113.1 fails
topology_note: Internal LAN: 192.168.1.0/24. Edge Router R1 WAN IP: 209.165.200.225/30 on Serial0/1/0.
show_output_evidence: PC1> ping 209.165.200.226 -> Request timed out; R1# show ip nat translations -> (empty); R1# show running-config | include ip nat -> ip nat inside source list 1 interface Serial0/1/0; R1# show access-lists 1 -> (empty/missing)
expected_fault: ACL 1 referenced by the NAT inside source command does not exist or has no permit entries for 192.168.1.0/24
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad ENSA Lab 5.4.3 (Troubleshoot NAT Configuration)

symptom: Only one internal host can access the Internet simultaneously; subsequent hosts time out
topology_note: Internal Subnet 192.168.10.0/24. Router R1 WAN interface Gi0/0/1 (Public IP 203.0.113.5).
show_output_evidence: R1# show ip nat translations -> Pro Inside global: 203.0.113.5, Inside local: 192.168.10.15; R1# show running-config | include ip nat -> ip nat inside source list 10 interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1
expected_fault: Missing 'overload' keyword on 'ip nat inside source list 10 interface Gi0/0/1', causing dynamic one-to-one NAT instead of PAT
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad ENSA Lab 5.4.3 & Cisco IOS NAT Configuration Guide

symptom: NAT translations not occurring; show ip nat translations is completely empty despite active traffic
topology_note: Router R1 connects LAN on Gi0/0 and ISP on Gi0/1. NAT overload configured for ACL 5.
show_output_evidence: R1# show running-config interface Gi0/0 -> (missing 'ip nat inside'); R1# show running-config interface Gi0/1 -> ip nat outside; R1# show ip nat translations -> (empty)
expected_fault: LAN interface Gi0/0 is missing the 'ip nat inside' configuration command
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad ENSA Lab 5.4.3 (Troubleshoot NAT)

symptom: Static NAT for DMZ Web Server fails; external users cannot access public IP 209.165.201.5
topology_note: DMZ Web Server private IP: 192.168.50.10. Public IP: 209.165.201.5. Edge Router R1.
show_output_evidence: R1# show running-config | include ip nat inside source static -> ip nat inside source static 192.168.50.100 209.165.201.5; R1# show ip interface brief | include 192.168.50 -> Server IP is 192.168.50.10
expected_fault: Static NAT command has typo in the local private IP address (192.168.50.100 instead of 192.168.50.10)
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad ENSA Lab 5.2.6 & 5.4.3

symptom: Wireless laptop cannot connect to Corporate SSID; receives 'Unable to connect to this network'
topology_note: Laptop-1 connecting to SSID 'Corp-Secure' managed by Cisco WLC / Lightweight AP.
show_output_evidence: Laptop Wi-Fi status: Disconnected; WLC# show wlan summary -> WLAN ID: 1, Profile Name: Corp-Secure, SSID: Corp-Secure, Status: Disabled
expected_fault: WLAN profile 'Corp-Secure' is disabled in the Wireless LAN Controller (WLC admin state is Disabled)
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad SRWE Lab 13.5.1 (Troubleshoot WLAN Issues on WLC)

symptom: Wireless clients associate with SSID 'Guest-WiFi' but fail to receive IP address from DHCP
topology_note: WLC with AP1. SSID 'Guest-WiFi' mapped to interface 'guest-interface' (VLAN 40).
show_output_evidence: Laptop> ipconfig -> 0.0.0.0; WLC# show interface summary -> guest-interface: VLAN 40, Port 1; S1# show vlan brief -> VLAN 40 does not exist on Switch S1
expected_fault: VLAN 40 is not created on the upstream distribution switch, dropping all tagged DHCP traffic from WLC interface
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad SRWE Lab 13.4.5 (Packet Tracer - Troubleshoot WLAN Issues)

symptom: Switch port shuts down immediately when user connects a new laptop; port LED amber
topology_note: User on Switch S1 interface FastEthernet0/10. Port security configured with max MAC 1.
show_output_evidence: S1# show interfaces Fa0/10 status -> Fa0/10 err-disabled; S1# show port-security interface Fa0/10 -> Port Security: Enabled, Port Status: Secure-shutdown, Violation Mode: Shutdown, Last Source Address: 0050.7966.6803
expected_fault: Port security violation triggered err-disabled state due to unauthorized MAC address on Fa0/10
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad SRWE Lab 10.4.3 (Troubleshoot LAN Security)

symptom: Spanning Tree loop detected; high CPU utilization and broadcast radiation across switch fabric
topology_note: Switch loop between S1, S2, S3 with redundant Gigabit uplinks. STP mode: PVST+.
show_output_evidence: S1# show spanning-tree summary -> UplinkFast: disabled, BPDU Guard: disabled; S2# show interfaces status -> Gi0/1 and Gi0/2 link lights flashing green rapidly; CPU 98%
expected_fault: STP was accidentally disabled globally on S2 ('no spanning-tree vlan 1-4094'), causing unmanaged Layer 2 broadcast storm
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad SRWE Lab 5.1.9 (Troubleshoot STP)

symptom: Subnet mask mismatch causes host to reject direct Layer 2 communication with neighbor
topology_note: Host A (192.168.1.10/24) and Host B (192.168.1.150/26) on the same VLAN and switch. Host B cannot ping Host A.
show_output_evidence: Host-A> ipconfig -> IP: 192.168.1.10, Mask: 255.255.255.0; Host-B> ipconfig -> IP: 192.168.1.150, Mask: 255.255.255.192. Host B considers 192.168.1.10 remote and sends ARP to nonexistent gateway.
expected_fault: Host B has incorrect subnet mask /26 (255.255.255.192) restricting its broadcast domain to .128-.191
reference_source_note: Adapted from NetAcad ITN Lab 11.5.5 (Subnetting Scenarios)
